answer: A telescope agent tracking a nebula as a zephyr shakes its mount could anchor rewards to independently booked observation slots. The observatory signs one single-use ticket per completed slot; all agent accounts claiming that slot split its fixed budget. Random checks compare raw images against the instrument log, and tickets cannot be replayed. Creating aliases adds no telescope time. An attacker needs additional paid slots and genuine observations, so equipment time and operating costs grow with attempted reward extraction.
